content:
**Largest Cosmetics & Beauty Companies (2023 ranking by revenue)**  

| Rank | Company | Headquarters | 2023 Revenue (beauty & personal‑care segment) | Year Founded | Brief note |
|------|---------|--------------|----------------------------------------------|--------------|------------|
| 1 | **L’Oréal** | Clichy, France | € 38 billion (global cosmetics & fragrance) | **1909** – founded by chemist **Eugène Schueller** | World’s biggest pure‑play beauty group; brands include Lancôme, Garnier, Maybelline, Kiehl’s, etc. |
| 2 | **Estée Lauder Companies** | New York, USA | US $ 17 billion | **1946** – founded by **Estée Lauder** and **Joseph Lauder** | Luxury‑focused portfolio (Estée Lauder, MAC, Clinique, Tom Ford Beauty, etc.). |
| 3 | **Unilever – Beauty & Personal Care** | London, UK & Rotterdam, NL | € 15 billion (beauty & personal‑care division) | **1929** – created by the merger of Lever Brothers (1885) and Margarine Unie (1927) | Brands such as Dove, Axe/Lynx, Sunsilk, Vaseline, Pond’s, and the “Luxury” arm (Dermablend, etc.). |
| 4 | **Procter & Gamble – Beauty & Grooming** | Cincinnati, USA | US $ 12 billion (beauty & grooming segment) | **1837** – founded by **William Procter** & **James Gamble** | Includes Olay, Pantene, Head & Shoulders, SK‑II (via partnership), and Gillette (grooming). |
| 5 | **Coty Inc.** | New York, USA | US $ 5.6 billion | **1904** – founded by **François Coty** | Holds a mix of prestige (Calvin Klein, Gucci, Marc Jacobs) and mass‑market (CoverGirl, Clairol) brands. |
| 6 | **Shiseido Company** | Tokyo, Japan | ¥ 1.2 trillion (~US $ 8 billion) | **1872** – founded by **Arinobu Tajima** (originally as a pharmacy) | Japan’s oldest cosmetics house; brands include Shiseido, NARS, Clé de Peau Beauté, and Drunk Elephant. |
| 7 | **Amorepacific Corp.** | Seoul, South Korea | KRW 6 trillion (~US $ 5 billion) | **1945** – founded as “Lucky Cosmetic” by **Suh Byung‑chul** | Home to Sulwhasoo, Laneige, Innisfree, Mamonde, and Etude House. |
| 8 | **Johnson & Johnson – Consumer Health & Beauty** | New Brunswick, USA | US $ 13 billion (consumer health & personal‑care) | **1886** – founded by **Robert Wood Johnson** & brothers | Brands include Neutrogena, Aveeno, Clean & Clear, and Johnson’s Baby. |
| 9 | **Avon Products** (now part of **Natura & Co**) | London, UK (operational HQ: New York, USA) | US $ 4 billion (beauty & personal‑care) | **1886** – founded as “California Perfume Company” by **David H. McConnell** | Historically a direct‑selling powerhouse; now integrated into Natura & Co. |
|10| **Revlon** (private) | New York, USA | US $ 2.5 billion (beauty) | **1932** – founded by **Charles Revson**, **Charles Laplante**, and **Joseph Revson** | Brands include Revlon, Almay, Elizabeth Arden, and the “American Crew” line. |

### How the list was built
* **Revenue basis** – Companies are ordered by the most recent (FY 2023) revenue attributable to their cosmetics/beauty & personal‑care divisions. For conglomerates (Unilever, Procter & Gamble, Johnson & Johnson) only the beauty‑related portion of the total group revenue is shown.  
* **Largest players** – The set reflects the global market share reported by industry analysts (e.g., Euromonitor, Statista, and company annual reports) and includes both pure‑play beauty groups (L’Oréal, Estée Lauder, Coty, Shiseido, Amorepacific) and diversified consumer‑goods giants whose beauty businesses rank among the world’s biggest.  
* **Founding year** – The year each firm was originally established (or the predecessor company that later became the modern brand) is taken from the companies’ own histories or reputable business references.

### Quick take‑aways
1. **Europe dominates the top spot** – L’Oréal (France) remains the clear leader, a position it has held for decades.  
2. **U.S. consumer‑goods giants are still major players** – Even though they are diversified, the beauty divisions of P&G, Unilever, and J&J each generate double‑digit‑billion‑dollar sales.  
3. **Asian innovators are rising fast** – Shiseido and Amorepacific have solidified their places among the top ten, and their growth rates (especially in Korea and China) outpace many legacy Western brands.  
4. **Heritage matters** – The oldest firms (Shiseido 1872, L’Oréal 1909, Coty 1904) have continually reinvented themselves, showing that longevity can coexist with market leadership.

If you need deeper details—such as brand‑level breakdowns, geographic revenue splits, or the latest 2024 forecasts—just let me know!
